stem: The device used to measure the strength of electric current flowing in a circuit is called a/an:
explanation: An ammeter measures current (in amperes) and is connected in series in a circuit, while a voltmeter measures potential difference (voltage) and is connected in parallel across a component.

stem: Household electrical wiring circuits are designed as parallel circuits rather than series circuits mainly because parallel wiring allows:

options.option_text: Each appliance to work independently at full voltage, and to be switched on/off without affecting others
All appliances to always turn on and off together
The total current to always be zero
Only one appliance to be used at a time in the whole house

explanation: Parallel wiring gives each appliance its own independent branch at full mains voltage, so switching one appliance on or off does not affect the others — essential for practical household use, unlike a series circuit where all components share the same current and depend on each other.
